stories.s: The Board of Supervisors declared a local emergency on Tuesday so the county’s emergency management office can prepare for a strong-to-very-strong El Niño with fewer bureaucratic hurdles. A new task force will coordinate with cities and agencies through March on risks such as flooding, landslides, coastal erosion, and power outages. Residents are urged to check their flood risk and sign up for SMC Alert, and most cities have opened sandbag sites.
stories.w: Peninsula cities including Redwood City and Menlo Park flooded in the 2022–23 storms, and early preparation can speed help and supplies this winter.

stories.t: Millbrae invites residents to test paid-parking options tonight
stories.s: Millbrae is drafting a downtown parking management plan and will let residents try two payment systems tonight from 5:30 to 8:30 p.m., one in the Chetcuti Room and one in the library. Rates, hours, zones, and equipment are still undecided and will be set at public City Council meetings. Parking revenue would go into a dedicated fund that can only be spent on parking.
stories.w: Paid parking would change the cost of shopping, dining, and commuting downtown, and resident feedback can shape the final plan.

stories.t: Judge limits DHS’s search for noncitizen voters in California and eight other states
stories.s: Federal Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín ordered the Department of Homeland Security on Wednesday to halt field steps such as interviews when it believes the target could be a U.S. citizen, citing flawed data known to include citizens. The order covers California and eight other states, takes effect Friday afternoon to allow an appeal, and lasts until after the midterms. Voting rights groups argued the effort was scaring citizens away from voting.
stories.w: The ruling is meant to protect eligible California voters, including naturalized citizens on the Peninsula, from being questioned before Nov. 3.

stories.t: California stages millions of sandbags and criticizes a federal pullback on disasters
stories.s: During Flood Preparedness Week, Governor Newsom’s office said the state has positioned 6.2 million sandbags, more than 52,000 feet of portable flood barriers, and 400,000 tons of rock at 70 sites ahead of El Niño. The office accused the Trump administration and FEMA of leaving states to handle disasters alone, without citing specific cuts. Residents are urged to use the state’s MyHazards tool to check flood risk at their address.
stories.w: State supplies and levee work back up local crews if Bay Area storms overwhelm county resources this winter.

stories.t: Today in sports: Lakers rout the Warriors in the opener; Valkyries fall behind in the Finals
stories.s: The Lakers beat the Warriors 127–105 on Wednesday as Luka Dončić scored 28 and Walker Kessler went 12-for-12 for 26; Stephen Curry led Golden State with 23, 16 of them in the first quarter, while Jimmy Butler III, Brandin Podziemski, Kristaps Porziņģis, and Moses Moody sat out hurt. The Valkyries lost Game 3 of the WNBA Finals 97–71 in Atlanta and trail 2–1, with Game 4 there on Saturday. Up next: the Warriors’ home opener against Memphis on Friday, the Quakes at FC Dallas on Saturday, and the 6–0 49ers at Atlanta on Sunday.

stories.t: NBA opening night: Edwards spoils Giannis’s Heat debut as stars return
stories.s: Anthony Edwards scored 45 as Minnesota beat Miami 131–106, spoiling Giannis Antetokounmpo’s 35-point Heat debut. Anthony Davis had 34 in his first game for Washington, Tyrese Haliburton returned from his Achilles injury to lift Indiana past New Orleans, and Kawhi Leonard scored 23 in his Toronto return. Kyrie Irving played for the first time in more than 19 months in Dallas’s loss to Houston.

stories.t: Nobody Wants This season 3 arrives on Netflix, and David Tennant joins Time
stories.s: Netflix releases all 10 episodes of Nobody Wants This season 3 today, as Joanne and Noah move in together. BritBox premieres season 3 of the prison drama Time with David Tennant and wraps season 1 of Cooper and Fry. Hulu also drops the true-crime series Swipe Right on the Devil.

stories.t: SF critic says no tech movie this season tops You Can See Everything
stories.s: The San Francisco Standard’s PST column argues that Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary You Can See Everything outclasses this fall’s wave of Silicon Valley films, including Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning and Alex Gibney’s four-hour Musk. The writer found the film hard to watch but impossible to look away from. The column pairs with a podcast episode built around a three-film tech-movie marathon.

stories.t: NASA lays out when SpaceX and Blue Origin landers should fly to the moon
stories.s: NASA’s lander program targets Artemis III for the third quarter of 2027, when four astronauts will test docking with both companies’ landers in Earth orbit, ahead of a crewed landing on Artemis IV in early 2028. SpaceX aims for an uncrewed Starship lunar landing demonstration by late 2027, and Blue Origin plans an uncrewed Blue Moon Mark 2 landing in early 2028. NASA scheduled a briefing for Friday on speeding up Artemis.

stories.t: AI helps uncover decades-old PHP flaws affecting much of the web
stories.s: The NSA warned Wednesday of two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind a large share of websites, that could let attackers reach a server’s files or database. Researchers at Calif, using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol, and Google’s Wiz team found the bugs, which date back to PHP 5, and patches are already out. Site owners, including WordPress users, should update to the current PHP version or work with their host.

stories.t: Walmart opens its store to AI shopping agents as Amazon blocks them
stories.s: Walmart launched Agent Gateway, which lets approved AI assistants search its inventory and buy items for shoppers without seeing their payment details. Starting next month, each agent gets its own profile in a customer’s account, with options to approve every purchase or set a spending limit. The approach contrasts with Amazon, which has begun blocking AI agents from shopping on its site.

stories.t: Today in history: Sartre turns down the Nobel Prize
stories.s: 1964: Jean-Paul Sartre was named winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature and declined it, the first person to refuse the award voluntarily.

stories.t: On this day in science: The first photocopy is made in Queens
stories.s: 1938: Inventor Chester Carlson and his assistant made the first xerographic copy in a rented lab in Astoria, New York; it simply read “10.-22.-38 Astoria.”

stories.t: Firsts in history: The first parachute jump from a balloon
stories.s: 1797: André-Jacques Garnerin cut loose from a hydrogen balloon high above Paris and floated down under a silk canopy, the first notable parachute descent.

stories.t: DA won’t file criminal charges against ousted Sheriff Christina Corpus
stories.s: San Mateo County District Attorney Steve Wagstaffe has closed his criminal investigation of former Sheriff Christina Corpus and her former chief of staff, finding no crime even though he called the 2024 arrest of a deputy union leader unjustified. Wagstaffe still plans to pursue four civil grand jury accusations against Corpus, which could bar her from holding elected office again. Supervisors removed her from office a year ago.
stories.w: The decision shapes the last chapter of a scandal that cost county taxpayers an undisclosed sum in investigations and legal fees.

stories.t: Trump’s approval hits a record low in CNN polling as Democrats lead the generic ballot
stories.s: A CNN/SSRS poll taken Oct. 15–18 found 32% of Americans approve of President Trump’s job performance, the lowest in CNN’s polling, with approval among Republicans at 74%. Registered voters favor Democrats 49% to 39% on the generic congressional ballot. The Nov. 3 midterms are less than two weeks away.
stories.w: Several competitive California House races on the Nov. 3 ballot will help decide which party controls Congress.

stories.t: California touts its first new steel mill in 50 years, powered by solar
stories.s: Governor Newsom highlighted Pacific Steel Group’s Mojave Micro Mill in Kern County, which will melt scrap steel in an electric furnace run by an on-site solar farm and batteries. The company has committed more than $540 million and expects about 700 jobs, aided by a $30 million state tax credit. The mill is set to open in 2027 and make about 380,000 tons of rebar a year.
stories.w: Locally made rebar could feed California construction and infrastructure projects, including Bay Area housing and transit work.

stories.t: SF supervisors seek emergency legal aid funding after an ICE detention in SoMa
stories.s: A coalition of San Francisco supervisors and immigrant legal groups rallied at City Hall on Tuesday for emergency money for legal services and the city’s rapid-response network. The call followed Monday’s detention of a man in South of Market by masked ICE officers, captured on video, in which he shouted that he is a U.S. citizen. No dollar amount or vote has been set.
stories.w: Immigrant families across the Peninsula rely on San Francisco’s legal aid network when enforcement actions happen nearby.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers improve to 6–0; Warriors open at the Lakers tonight
stories.s: The 49ers beat Washington 23–17 on Monday Night Football at Levi’s Stadium behind two Christian McCaffrey touchdowns and a George Kittle scoring catch, with Brock Purdy throwing for 264 yards; they visit Atlanta on Sunday. The Warriors open their season tonight at the Lakers, and the Earthquakes, already playoff-bound, play at FC Dallas on Saturday. In the WNBA Finals, the Valkyries lost Game 2 to Atlanta 79–65 on Monday, tying the series 1–1 before Game 3 tonight in Atlanta.

stories.t: Giants weigh free-agent arms after a 97-loss season
stories.s: With four young starters recovering from Tommy John surgery and a staff ERA that ranked 23rd, the Giants are expected to shop for pitching this winter, and Buster Posey has called the bullpen a priority. MLB.com lists closers David Bednar and Raisel Iglesias and starters Michael King and former Giant Kevin Gausman among possible targets. Free agency opens after the World Series.

stories.t: The Terminal List returns and Slow Horses wraps season 6 today
stories.s: Prime Video drops all eight episodes of The Terminal List season 2, and Apple TV airs the Slow Horses season 6 finale along with the season 2 premiere of Where’s Wanda?. Disney+ adds the live-action Moana after its summer theatrical run. Tonight ABC airs a two-hour CMA tribute to Dolly Parton that benefits her Imagination Library.

stories.t: Jon Stewart extends his Daily Show deal through the 2028 election
stories.s: Skydance Television said Monday that Jon Stewart will keep hosting The Daily Show on Comedy Central through December 2028 and remain an executive producer. He will continue hosting on Mondays while the news team rotates through the rest of the week. Stewart returned to the show in 2024 after first hosting from 1999 to 2015.

stories.t: SpaceX will try to catch both Starship stages on its next test flight
stories.s: Elon Musk said on SpaceX’s quarterly earnings call that Starship Flight 15, expected in November, will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and, for the first time, the Ship upper stage with the launch tower’s arms. Success would mean an orbital rocket fully recovered for reuse. SpaceX also reported $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue.

stories.t: Japan launches MMX to bring back samples from Mars’ moon Phobos
stories.s: JAXA’s Martian Moons eXploration probe lifted off on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima on Monday and is due at Mars in August 2027. It plans to land on Phobos twice, carry a small French-German rover, and return a sample to Earth in 2031. NASA contributed instruments and will receive part of the sample.

stories.t: ChatGPT adds a way to lock private chats behind a PIN or Face ID
stories.s: OpenAI began rolling out Locked Chats on Tuesday for most ChatGPT plans, including Free, letting users hide chosen conversations behind a four-digit PIN or Face ID or Touch ID. Locked chats move to their own section and stay out of search and regular memory. Resetting the PIN permanently deletes them, and the feature doesn’t add encryption.

stories.t: Federal agencies ordered to remove DeepSeek AI from their systems
stories.s: The Department of Homeland Security directed federal civilian agencies to stop buying DeepSeek products and remove them from existing systems, including third-party tools built on its models. DHS cited the risk that Chinese authorities could access government data. Agencies can request exceptions, and China’s Foreign Ministry objected to the move.

stories.t: Today in history: The Guggenheim’s spiral opens
stories.s: 1959: The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, Frank Lloyd Wright’s spiraling landmark, opened to the public in New York City.

stories.t: On this day in science: Alfred Nobel is born
stories.s: 1833: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite and later funded the Nobel Prizes, was born in Stockholm.

stories.t: Firsts in history: Magellan finds a way into the Pacific
stories.s: 1520: Ferdinand Magellan’s fleet reached the strait at the tip of South America that now bears his name, opening the first known sea route from the Atlantic to the Pacific.

stories.t: Sequoia district students push back on an all-day phone ban
stories.s: In a Sequoia Union High School District survey, 94% of 1,267 students opposed a bell-to-bell phone ban, many saying they need to reach parents, while most staff favored one and 62% of parents supported it. Current rules restrict phones during class through the end of this school year but allow them at lunch and between periods. District staff will bring a recommended policy for 2027–28 to the board on Nov. 18.
stories.w: School phone limits are being debated across Peninsula districts, and Sequoia’s decision will shape daily rules for thousands of San Mateo County teens.

stories.t: California wins a $6 million settlement from 23andMe over its data breach
stories.s: Attorney General Rob Bonta announced Monday a $6 million settlement with 23andMe over claims it failed to protect customers’ genetic and personal data in a 2023 breach affecting nearly 7 million U.S. users, then misled them about how serious it was. The company, renamed Chrome Holding Co., filed for bankruptcy in 2025, and its assets went to the nonprofit 23andMe Research Institute. Customers can ask the institute to delete their data and samples and withdraw research consent.
stories.w: Bay Area residents who used 23andMe can request that their genetic data and samples be deleted.

stories.t: Federal prosecutors charge 28 California green card holders with illegal voting
stories.s: Federal prosecutors charged 28 lawful permanent residents across California, from Los Angeles County to Sacramento, with illegally registering or voting; 22 are accused of voting in at least one election, including the June primary. Attorney General Rob Bonta called the cases tiny against about 23 million registered voters, and Gov. Gavin Newsom called the effort an attempt to suppress voters. It comes days after federal officials sued to block counting of up to 20,000 California ballots.
stories.w: The charges add pressure on county election offices statewide, including San Mateo County’s, in the final two weeks before Nov. 3.

stories.t: Detained Central Valley farmworkers are being denied lawyers, advocates say
stories.s: Immigration attorneys say people swept up in a federal enforcement surge in the Central Valley since Oct. 5, which observers estimate has led to as many as 200 arrests, have repeatedly been denied access to lawyers at ICE facilities in Fresno and Bakersfield. Some detainees were quickly moved as far as Texas, and attorneys say dozens are effectively unaccounted for. ICE declined to discuss specific operations.
stories.w: Bay Area legal aid groups are watching closely amid fears the operation could spread to the region.

stories.t: San Francisco keeps its Flock cameras as other Bay Area cities drop them
stories.s: Mountain View, Santa Cruz, El Cerrito and other cities have dropped or scaled back Flock license-plate cameras over privacy concerns, but San Francisco is keeping its roughly 400 cameras. Mayor Daniel Lurie cut data retention to 30 days after police disclosed improper searches by outside agencies, and the city will weigh renewing the contract in February 2027.
stories.w: Peninsula drivers heading into San Francisco pass these cameras, and how long the city keeps plate data affects their privacy too.

stories.t: SF prosecutors charge a construction company over a 2023 trench death
stories.s: San Francisco prosecutors filed felony involuntary manslaughter charges Monday against D’Arcy & Harty Construction and three of its employees over a 2023 trench collapse in the Lower Haight that killed a 24-year-old worker on a city sewer project. Cal/OSHA had found the trench was not properly supported. A preliminary hearing is set for Nov. 14.
stories.w: Criminal charges over a workplace death on a city-contracted job are rare and put contractors across the region on notice.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers move to 6-0, Valkyries’ Finals series is even
stories.s: The 49ers held off Washington 23-17 on Monday Night Football to stay unbeaten. The Valkyries fell 79-65 to the Atlanta Dream in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals, the Dream’s first Finals win in franchise history, and the series is tied 1-1 with Game 3 on Wednesday at 5 p.m. Pacific. The Warriors open their season Wednesday at the Lakers, and the Earthquakes visit FC Dallas on Saturday.

stories.t: McCaffrey scores twice as the 49ers hold off Washington to stay perfect
stories.s: Christian McCaffrey ran for two touchdowns and caught nine passes, and George Kittle scored on an 11-yard catch as the 49ers built a 20-3 halftime lead and held on to beat Washington 23-17 at Levi’s Stadium. Playing without Nick Bosa, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, the defense held Washington to 53 rushing yards and sealed it with a late fourth-down stop and a game-ending sack. Mike Evans had 94 yards on three catches before leaving before halftime; San Francisco (6-0) plays at Atlanta on Sunday at 10 a.m.

stories.t: Lil Jon’s memoir, with deep Bay Area roots, is out today
stories.s: Lil Jon’s memoir, I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me, written with Paul Cantor, comes out today. It traces his Atlanta upbringing and rise in the music business and details his Bay Area ties, including Too Short buying him and the East Side Boyz out of a bad record deal and his work with E-40 on My Ghetto Report Card.

stories.t: Coming Friday: new albums from John Legend, Lisa and Michael Kiwanuka
stories.s: Friday’s releases include John Legend’s Muse, Lisa’s Press Play, Michael Kiwanuka’s Fudge, Brothers Osborne’s Watertown and Polyphia’s Be Not Afraid. Also due are Offset’s GMFU, Hilary Duff’s Holiday Things and Tony Iommi’s From the Dark.

stories.t: AI assistant Anna aims to tame working parents’ busy schedules
stories.s: Anna, an AI personal assistant for working parents built by former Meta and Atlassian product leader Dilani Kahawala, responds to voice prompts, sorts incoming school and family messages, flags calendar conflicts and turns information into tasks. The company says its August public launch spread quickly among parents after months of near-daily beta use.

stories.t: Today in history: Sydney Opera House opens
stories.s: 1973: Queen Elizabeth II opened the Sydney Opera House, whose sail-like shells became one of the world’s most recognizable buildings.

stories.t: On this day in science: Monterey Bay Aquarium opens on Cannery Row
stories.s: 1984: The Monterey Bay Aquarium opened in a former sardine cannery on California’s Cannery Row, showcasing the ocean life of the bay just outside its walls.

stories.t: Firsts in history: A US spacecraft grabs a piece of an asteroid
stories.s: 2020: NASA’s OSIRIS-REx briefly touched the asteroid Bennu and collected rock and dust, the first time a US spacecraft had sampled an asteroid.

stories.t: Today is the last day to register to vote online for Nov. 3
stories.s: Eligible Californians can register or update their registration online at registertovote.ca.gov until midnight tonight for the Nov. 3 general election. After that, they can still use same-day conditional registration in person at their county elections office or any vote center through Election Day; those ballots are counted once the county verifies them. Voters can check their status at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov.
stories.w: San Mateo County residents who have moved or never registered can still do it from home today and skip a trip to a vote center later.

stories.t: What to do if your mail ballot hasn’t arrived
stories.s: Bay Area counties had to begin mailing ballots by Oct. 5, so voters still waiting should check the state’s voter status page or the Where’s My Ballot tool. Voters who moved should re-register at their new address, and others can request a replacement from their county, though counties stop mailing replacements six days before Election Day and after that issue them in person. More early voting locations open starting Oct. 24 and again Oct. 31.
stories.w: With some San Mateo County ballots stolen from a Daly City post office last week, checking your ballot’s status is a quick safeguard.

stories.t: No Kings protests turn into an early-voting push
stories.s: Thousands turned out Saturday for No Kings Vote Early events in cities from Washington, D.C., to Minneapolis, as organizers focused on turnout, early voting and training poll watchers. The coalition, which includes Indivisible, the ACLU and Black Voters Matter, called the effort nonpartisan and barred endorsements and current candidates from speaking.
stories.w: With San Mateo County ballots already in mailboxes, groups across the spectrum are focused on getting voters to return them early.

stories.t: Weekend recap: Valkyries strike first, Quakes clinch, 49ers play tonight
stories.s: Friday: the Warriors hosted Portland in a preseason game at Chase Center. Saturday: the Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, and the Earthquakes tied Nashville 1-1 to clinch their first playoff spot since 2023. This week: the 49ers (5-0) host Washington tonight at 5:15, the Warriors open Wednesday at the Lakers and host Memphis on Friday, the Quakes visit FC Dallas on Saturday and the 49ers play at Atlanta Sunday at 10 a.m.

stories.t: 49ers put their perfect start on the line in their first prime-time game
stories.s: The unbeaten 49ers host the Washington Commanders tonight at Levi’s Stadium in their first prime-time game of the season, on ESPN and ABC at 5:15 p.m., during the team’s Alumni Weekend. They will be without Nick Bosa and Deebo Samuel, with Mike Evans and Christian Kirk questionable. Punter Corliss Waitman was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his work in the win at Seattle.

stories.t: Street Fighter wins the weekend with a $30.8 million opening
stories.s: Street Fighter led the weekend with about $30.8 million from 3,575 theaters. You Can See Everything was second with $15.6 million, holdover Other Mommy took third with $8.2 million, and newcomers Whalefall ($7.8 million) and Sense and Sensibility ($7.2 million) rounded out the top five.

stories.t: You Can See Everything posts the weekend’s best per-theater average
stories.s: Playing in just 855 theaters, You Can See Everything averaged about $18,247 per location, more than double Street Fighter’s roughly $8,600. The Indian sequel Jailer 2 also opened in the top 10 with $3.1 million from 800 screens, and the top 20 films together grossed about $100.9 million.

stories.t: SpaceX readies Bandwagon-5 rideshare and Starfall capsule for Tuesday launch
stories.s: SpaceX is targeting 7:04 a.m. EDT (4:04 a.m. PDT) Tuesday for a Falcon 9 launch from Cape Canaveral carrying 31 customer payloads on its Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission. The flight also carries the company’s uncrewed Starfall reentry capsule on its second trip to space.

stories.t: Today in history: Cornwallis surrenders at Yorktown
stories.s: 1781: Lord Cornwallis surrendered his British army to American and French forces at Yorktown, Virginia, effectively ending major fighting in the Revolutionary War.

stories.t: On this day in science: A doctor sets out to prove castaways can survive
stories.s: 1952: French physician Alain Bombard left the Canary Islands in a small inflatable boat, testing his theory that shipwreck survivors could live off the sea.

stories.t: Firsts in history: The Supreme Court gets its first chief justice
stories.s: 1789: John Jay was sworn in as the first chief justice of the US Supreme Court.

stories.t: AC Transit details deep cuts if the Bay Area transit tax fails
stories.s: The Regional Transit Measure on the Nov. 3 ballot would add a half-cent sales tax in San Mateo, Alameda, Contra Costa and Santa Clara counties and a one-cent tax in San Francisco, raising about $1 billion a year for 14 years for agencies including BART and Caltrain. AC Transit says that without it, it would cut service 16%, pull 100 buses and lay off up to 300 workers starting in June 2027. Its board expects to consider a final contingency plan on Dec. 9.
stories.w: San Mateo County voters help decide this measure, which would fund the BART and Caltrain service Millbrae riders rely on.

stories.t: Rumors of a statewide ICE operation spread as Central Valley arrests climb
stories.s: Advocates say more than 100 farmworkers and others have been detained in the Central Valley this week, while unverified reports of a 45-day operation targeting San Francisco, Los Angeles and San Diego have spread; Bay Area rapid-response groups say they have not seen a local surge. Gov. Gavin Newsom urged residents to know their rights. A state law bars arrests within 200 feet of polling places on Election Day, though it does not cover early voting.
stories.w: Peninsula immigrant families and advocates are preparing for possible enforcement, and the polling-place protections matter as voting gets underway.

stories.t: San José says it’s ready for a strong El Niño winter
stories.s: Federal forecasters give an 83% chance of a historic El Niño from October through December, and San José says upgrades since the 2017 Coyote Creek flood, funded partly by voter-approved Measure T, leave it far better prepared. Valley Water has built more than 8,000 feet of flood walls along Coyote Creek and recently awarded a $100 million contract for the next phase. The City Council will get an update on its highest-risk flood sites in the coming weeks.
stories.w: The same storm pattern threatens the Peninsula, so this is a good time to clear gutters and storm drains before the rains arrive.

stories.t: Unruly passenger forces a Singapore-bound flight back to SFO
stories.s: Singapore Airlines flight SQ31 returned to SFO on Wednesday night, about nine hours after departing, after the airline said a passenger became unruly and injured himself. Passengers got off while the plane refueled, and it left for Singapore around 11:20 p.m. with a new crew. Social media claims of an arrest have not been confirmed by the airline.
stories.w: Turnbacks like this can leave SFO travelers rebooking long-haul connections, a reminder to keep airline alerts on for overnight flights.

stories.t: Today in sports: Valkyries take Game 1, Quakes clinch, 49ers host Washington Monday
stories.s: The Valkyries closed on a 17-6 run to beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals and lead the best-of-seven series 1-0. The Earthquakes drew 1-1 with Nashville SC, enough to clinch a playoff spot. The 5-0 49ers host Washington on Monday Night Football at 5:15 p.m., and the Warriors open their season Wednesday at the Lakers.

stories.t: Quakes clinch first playoff berth since 2023 with draw against Nashville
stories.s: Preston Judd’s 70th-minute goal, set up by Eduard Löwen, answered Hany Mukhtar’s first-half strike as San Jose tied league leader Nashville 1-1 at PayPal Park on Saturday and clinched a place in the MLS Cup Playoffs. The Quakes (13-8-9, 48 points) sit fourth in the West and are unbeaten in nine league matches. They visit FC Dallas next Saturday at 7:30 p.m.

stories.t: Nick Bosa and Deebo Samuel ruled out for Monday night against Washington
stories.s: The 49ers ruled out defensive lineman Nick Bosa (knee, calf), receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring), linebacker Garret Wallow and safety Marques Sigle for Monday’s game against Washington. Receivers Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Christian Kirk (calf) are questionable, while fullback Kyle Juszczyk is expected back after missing Week 5. Final decisions come 90 minutes before kickoff at Levi’s Stadium.

stories.t: Street Fighter wins Friday at the box office
stories.s: Street Fighter earned about $13 million on its opening day from 3,575 theaters, well ahead of the field. You Can See Everything took in $5.5 million from just 855 theaters, while fellow newcomers Sense and Sensibility ($3.3 million) and Whalefall ($3.1 million) also landed in the top five. Weekend estimates arrive today.

stories.t: Fontaines D.C., The Avalanches and Gucci Mane lead Friday’s new albums
stories.s: Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. released Dopamine Chamber on XL Recordings, its follow-up to 2024’s Romance, led by the single Marianne. Also out Friday: The Avalanches’ No Bad Memories, Gucci Mane’s Against All Odds, Eels’ Cookie Happened, Lucky Daye’s Aloud! and Max Richter’s While the Flood Rages.

stories.t: Crystal Lake, A24’s Friday the 13th prequel series, is streaming on Peacock
stories.s: Peacock released all eight episodes of Crystal Lake on Thursday, a prequel to the Friday the 13th films starring Linda Cardellini as Pamela Voorhees. Produced by A24 with Brad Caleb Kane as showrunner, the series arrives on Sky and NOW in the U.K. and Ireland on Monday.

stories.t: Blue Origin plans more Florida launch pads to speed up New Glenn flights
stories.s: Blue Origin says it will build more Space Coast launch pads modeled on its Cape Canaveral complex, add two landing ships and spend $330 million expanding its Rocket Park factory to build up to 150 upper stages a year. The company is still recovering from a May test-fire explosion and has asked the FAA to raise its permitted launches at LC-36A from 12 to 50 a year; a virtual public hearing is set for Oct. 22.

stories.t: Today in history: The US flag rises over Alaska
stories.s: 1867: The American flag was raised at Sitka as Russia formally handed over Alaska, completing a purchase once mocked as “Seward’s Folly.”

stories.t: On this day in science: A cat named Félicette rides a rocket
stories.s: 1963: France launched Félicette on a suborbital rocket flight, making her the first cat in space; she returned safely by parachute.

stories.t: Firsts in history: The first all-woman spacewalk
stories.s: 2019: NASA astronauts Christina Koch and Jessica Meir stepped outside the International Space Station together for the first spacewalk carried out entirely by women.

stories.t: California sues to keep the National Archives in San Bruno
stories.s: Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a federal lawsuit Wednesday to stop the National Archives from closing its San Bruno facility, which holds more than 75,000 cubic feet of federal records from Northern California and the Pacific region. The suit says the agency skipped required public and tribal consultation; the records, including immigration, court and Japanese American incarceration files, would be moved to sites in Riverside, Colorado, Maryland, Texas and Missouri. Rep. Kevin Mullin has introduced a bill requiring congressional approval before such closures.
stories.w: The archive sits next door to Millbrae and is a key resource for Peninsula families tracing immigration and family records, fewer than 4% of which are digitized.

stories.t: Justice Department sues California to set aside 20,000 mailed ballots
stories.s: The U.S. Justice Department sued California and Los Angeles County election officials on Thursday, asking a federal court to set aside, and block the counting of, mail ballots sent to more than 20,000 voters it says are likely noncitizens. Secretary of State Shirley Weber said the state has not seen data backing the claim and will not disenfranchise voters on that basis, and legal experts note similar federal suits have failed. Ballots are already out statewide ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
stories.w: Nothing has changed yet for San Mateo County voters, but the case could affect how ballots are handled statewide in the final weeks before Election Day.

stories.t: Construction begins on 501 apartments at Redwood City’s Elco Yards
stories.s: High Street Residential has started building two apartment buildings with 501 units at Elco Yards in Redwood City, with completion expected in 2029. The El Camino Real building will include about 5,300 square feet of ground-floor retail. The groundbreaking follows a 2025 City Council vote that reduced the number of units reserved for lower-income households, a change the developer said it needed to make the project financially feasible.
stories.w: New homes on the El Camino corridor add supply in a county with steep rents, though fewer will be priced for low-income households than first planned.

stories.t: California gas averages $6.26 as the Iran war drives prices up nationwide
stories.s: California drivers are paying an average of $6.26 a gallon, far above the $4.33 national average, after Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz sent oil prices soaring. U.S. prices have risen $1.35 a gallon since the war began, and the national average hit a record in September. Democrats are now running ads blaming Republicans for the spike, while Republicans point to California’s gas tax and climate rules.
stories.w: Higher pump prices hit Peninsula commuters directly and are becoming a central issue in California’s competitive House races.

stories.t: Today in sports: Quakes chase a playoff spot, 49ers prep for Monday night
stories.s: The Warriors hosted Portland at Chase Center on Friday night in a preseason game, playing without Kristaps Porzingis, Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody; their regular season opens Wednesday at the Lakers. The Earthquakes host league-leading Nashville SC tonight at 7:30 at PayPal Park, and the 5-0 49ers host Washington on Monday Night Football at 5:15 p.m. The Golden State Valkyries also open the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream today.

stories.t: Earthquakes can clinch first playoff berth since 2023 against Nashville
stories.s: San Jose (13-8-8) is fourth in the Western Conference and unbeaten in eight league matches, and a win over Nashville SC tonight would clinch its first playoff trip since 2023. Nashville (20-3-6) is one win from wrapping up the Supporters’ Shield. The Quakes earned a 1-1 draw at Real Salt Lake on Wednesday on Jack Jasinski’s stoppage-time equalizer, with Angus Gunn making six saves.

stories.t: 49ers open practice window for Christian Kirk ahead of Washington
stories.s: The 49ers promoted defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to the active roster and opened the practice window for receiver Christian Kirk as they prepare for Monday’s home game against Washington. They also added linebacker Eugene Asante to the practice squad. San Francisco is 5-0 and in first place in the NFC West after last Sunday’s 32-29 win at Seattle.

stories.t: Street Fighter brings the video game brawlers to theaters
stories.s: Paramount and Legendary’s Street Fighter, based on Capcom’s fighting games, opened Friday in theaters and IMAX after debuting in several overseas markets earlier in the week. Directed by Kitao Sakurai, the PG-13 film stars Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Jason Momoa and David Dastmalchian, and carries a reported $82 million budget. Weekend estimates arrive Sunday.

stories.t: Gaza-raised, Bay Area-based rapper MC Abdul releases his debut album
stories.s: MC Abdul, an 18-year-old Palestinian rapper who grew up in Gaza and now lives in the Bay Area, released his nine-track debut album, Day by Day, Shway Shway, on Friday through San Francisco label EMPIRE. Producer Illmind built its Afrobeats-inspired beats. He performs today at Palestine Culture Day in Redwood City.

stories.t: Black Panther Party’s 60th anniversary celebrations wrap up in Oakland
stories.s: Events marking 60 years since the Black Panther Party’s founding continue this weekend, with workshops, a 25th-anniversary screening of A Huey P. Newton Story and an anniversary gala tonight featuring co-founder Bobby Seale. A free community day with live music follows Sunday at Bobby Hutton Park in West Oakland.

stories.t: Falcon 9 launches a classified Space Force payload from Vandenberg
stories.s: A SpaceX Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base on the Central Coast at 5:01 p.m. Thursday carrying a classified payload for the U.S. Space Force on the USSF-481 mission. No details about the satellite’s purpose were released.

stories.t: CHP holds driver, not Tesla, responsible after sleeping motorist on Full Self-Driving hits patrol car
stories.s: The CHP says a driver using Tesla’s Full Self-Driving system told officers he was asleep when his car struck a patrol car on I-80 in Fairfield late Tuesday, seriously injuring two officers who have since been released from the hospital. The agency stressed that FSD is a driver-assistance system that requires constant supervision and is holding the driver responsible. Investigators will pull the car’s data and may ask the DMV to revoke his license.

stories.t: Today in history: Burgoyne surrenders at Saratoga
stories.s: 1777: British general John Burgoyne surrendered his army after the Second Battle of Saratoga, a turning point that helped bring France into the American Revolution on the colonists’ side.

stories.t: On this day in science: Einstein arrives in America for good
stories.s: 1933: Albert Einstein arrived in the United States and settled in Princeton, New Jersey, where he spent the rest of his career and never returned to Europe.

stories.t: Firsts in history: The world’s first full-scale atomic power station opens
stories.s: 1956: Queen Elizabeth II opened Calder Hall in Cumbria, England, the first nuclear power station to deliver electricity to a national grid on a commercial scale.

stories.t: Ballots stolen from a Daly City post office; San Mateo County voters urged to check theirs
stories.s: An unknown number of San Mateo County vote-by-mail ballots were in mail stolen from a Daly City post office, and the county elections office is investigating with the US Postal Service after learning of the theft Wednesday. Voters who are worried can request a replacement ballot online by Oct. 27 or in person at any vote center, and can track their ballot through the state’s free Where’s My Ballot service.
stories.w: Any San Mateo County voter, including in Millbrae, can sign up for ballot tracking to confirm their ballot is mailed, received and counted.

stories.t: Southbound 101 closes in San Francisco this weekend as the Valkyries host the WNBA Finals
stories.s: Caltrans is closing southbound Highway 101 near Hospital Curve from 11 p.m. Friday to 6 a.m. Monday. The closure overlaps the Golden State Valkyries’ WNBA Finals home games against the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center, at 12:30 p.m. Saturday and 5 p.m. Monday, and Caltrain is urging fans to ride to Fourth and King, where Muni light rail is free with a game ticket.
stories.w: Drivers heading home to the Peninsula from San Francisco should expect detours and delays all weekend; Caltrain from Millbrae avoids the closure.

stories.t: BART will swap trains for buses between Daly City and 24th Street on Nov. 14–15
stories.s: BART will halt trains between 24th St. Mission and Daly City the weekend of Nov. 14–15 to install equipment for its new train control system, with SamTrans express buses and Muni shuttles filling the gap. The Green Line will be canceled, Red Line trains will turn back at 24th St. Mission, trains between Daly City and Millbrae will run every 15 minutes, and riders south of 24th St. should plan on delays of up to 30 minutes.
stories.w: Millbrae and SFO riders heading into San Francisco that weekend will have to switch to a bus at Daly City and should budget extra time.

stories.t: California’s next governor faces hard choices on Medi-Cal
stories.s: Medi-Cal covers about 13.6 million Californians, roughly 1 in 3, and now costs $222 billion a year, more than 40% of state spending, just as federal cuts of more than $900 billion over a decade begin. Republican Steve Hilton wants to narrow eligibility and end coverage for immigrants without legal status, while Democrat Xavier Becerra pledges to shield residents from federal cuts but hasn’t said how the state would pay. An enrollment freeze for undocumented adults and new monthly premiums take effect next year.
stories.w: About a third of Californians rely on Medi-Cal, so the governor’s race will shape coverage for many San Mateo County families.

stories.t: Teen gunman kills three children and a teacher at an Oregon elementary school
stories.s: A 16-year-old shot his way through locked doors at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday, killing three children and a teacher before a civilian who followed him inside shot and killed him, police said. A 7-year-old and another teacher were critically wounded, and all Bend-La Pine schools are closed today.
stories.w: The attack in central Oregon is likely to renew questions about school safety plans in districts across the West Coast, including the Bay Area.

stories.t: Today in sports: Quakes host league-leading Nashville Saturday; 49ers get ready for Washington
stories.s: Fresh off Wednesday’s stoppage-time draw in Utah, the Earthquakes, unbeaten in eight and fourth in the West, host Nashville SC at PayPal Park on Saturday with a playoff berth in sight. The 5–0 49ers host Washington on Monday night without suspended linebacker Dre Greenlaw, the Warriors play their final preseason game before Wednesday’s opener at the Lakers, and the Bay Area’s Valkyries open the WNBA Finals at Chase Center on Saturday.

stories.t: New this weekend: “Street Fighter” in theaters, Chris Evans in Netflix’s “Sacrifice,” and a new Fontaines D.C. album
stories.s: In theaters, Paramount’s Street Fighter opens after $4 million in Thursday previews, alongside Whalefall, A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything and Sense and Sensibility. On streaming, Netflix has Sacrifice with Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy, Prime Video has Stanley Tucci’s Mona Lisa heist Masterplan, Apple TV has the Everest drama Tenzing, and Tulsa King season 4 starts on Paramount+. New albums include Fontaines D.C.’s Dopamine Chamber, Babehoven’s I See Them, I See Me and The Avalanches’ No Bad Memories.

stories.t: Fontaines D.C. turn darker and more reflective on “Dopamine Chamber”
stories.s: The Dublin band’s fifth album, the follow-up to Romance, takes a darker, more reflective look at modern life and tops Radio Milwaukee’s picks for the week. Other standouts include June McDoom’s harmony-rich folk record Follow the Light, Babehoven’s I See Them, I See Me and new releases from Rachel Chinouriri, Eels and HAAI.

stories.t: Cargo Dragon docks at the space station with its last new solar arrays
stories.s: SpaceX’s CRS-35 Dragon, which launched Tuesday from Cape Canaveral, docked with the International Space Station at 7:27 a.m. Pacific on Thursday after a roughly 51-hour chase. It delivered more than 6,300 pounds of food, research gear and hardware, including the last of eight upgraded solar panels, and will stay about a month before returning to Earth.

stories.t: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope makes TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026
stories.s: TIME named the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope to its annual list of the year’s most groundbreaking inventions. Roman launched Aug. 30 and is partway through a roughly three-month trip to its final orbit while engineers test its instruments, with first images expected by early 2027. The telescope will survey huge areas of sky to study dark energy, dark matter and planets around other stars.

stories.t: GitHub’s AI Scan for pull requests is now generally available
stories.s: GitHub’s AI Scan automatically checks code changes in pull requests for security flaws in languages its CodeQL engine doesn’t yet cover, such as PHP, shell scripts, Terraform and Dockerfiles, and can suggest fixes. It’s available for public repositories and requires GitHub Code Security or Advanced Security for private ones; its findings are advisory and don’t block merges.

stories.t: Today in history: The Cardiff Giant fools a nation
stories.s: 1869: Workers in upstate New York “discovered” the Cardiff Giant, a supposed petrified man that drew paying crowds before it was exposed as a hoax.

stories.t: On this day in science: Ether makes surgery painless
stories.s: 1846: Dentist William T.G. Morton gave the first public demonstration of ether as a general anesthetic at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston.

stories.t: Firsts in history: The first U.S. birth control clinic opens
stories.s: 1916: Margaret Sanger opened the first birth control clinic in the United States, in Brooklyn, New York.

stories.t: Inflation jumps to 3.7% as gasoline prices soar
stories.s: Consumer prices rose 0.6% in September and 3.7% over the past year, the Labor Department reported Wednesday, as gasoline climbed 9.1% in a single month and 34.2% from a year earlier. Prices excluding food and energy rose a milder 2.6% over the year, food prices were flat for the month, and shelter costs rose 0.4%.
stories.w: With gasoline up about a third from last year, fill-ups are taking a much bigger bite out of Peninsula household budgets.

stories.t: PG&E widens its wildfire-safety shutoff to about 88,000 customers
stories.s: PG&E expanded its shutoff plan to about 88,000 customers in 29 counties, including 5,500 who rely on power for medical needs, as a dry offshore wind event set in Wednesday evening. Outages could last through Saturday afternoon, and the utility planned more than 40 resource centers offering charging, Wi-Fi and water. Bay Area counties on the list include Alameda, Contra Costa, Napa, Solano and Sonoma; San Mateo is not.
stories.w: Peninsula homes aren’t slated for shutoffs, but the dry winds raise fire danger across the region, so avoid anything that could spark a fire outdoors.

stories.t: Millbrae reopens Aviador Bridge after emergency repairs
stories.s: The 1947 bridge carrying Aviador Avenue over the Highline Canal, a second route in and out of the Bayside Manor neighborhood, reopened Oct. 8 to cars, bikes and pedestrians after crews installed temporary steel supports inside its deteriorating culverts. It had been closed since June 1. The city still plans a full replacement, estimated at $4 million to $5 million, and is seeking grants to pay for it.
stories.w: Bayside Manor residents have their second way in and out back before winter storms arrive.

stories.t: California’s billionaire tax would send most of its money to health care
stories.s: Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the roughly 200 Californians worth at least $1 billion, with 90% of the money going to health care, such as covering people cut from Medi-Cal by new federal work rules. Gov. Gavin Newsom and both major candidates for governor oppose it, and Propositions 41 and 42, backed by more than $100 million from Google co-founder Sergey Brin, would restrict new wealth taxes. September polls showed support between 45% and 52%.
stories.w: The vote could help decide whether San Mateo County residents who lose Medi-Cal under federal cuts get state-funded coverage.

stories.t: Caltrain strikes a pedestrian in Menlo Park and a car in Palo Alto
stories.s: A person was struck and killed by a Caltrain near Alma Street and Sherwood Way in Menlo Park around 9 a.m. Wednesday. That evening, around 6:15 p.m., a train hit a car stopped on the tracks along Alma Street in Palo Alto; police said the driver had minor injuries.
stories.w: Incidents on the tracks can ripple delays along the Peninsula line, so Millbrae riders should check Caltrain alerts before heading out.

stories.t: Iran reportedly sinks two cargo ships near the Strait of Hormuz
stories.s: Iranian attacks reportedly sank two Emirati cargo ships in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, after Iran struck at least 24 vessels between Sept. 28 and Oct. 11, according to the Critical Threats Project and the Institute for the Study of War. An Iranian official said Tehran aims to keep oil prices high to pressure President Trump before the midterms, and Houthi missiles hit a Saudi Aramco base on Tuesday.
stories.w: Shipping attacks in the Gulf help explain why gas is so expensive at California pumps.

stories.t: Today in sports: Quakes grab a stoppage-time draw in Salt Lake to stay unbeaten in eight
stories.s: Substitute Jack Jasinski scored in second-half stoppage time to earn San Jose a 1–1 draw at Real Salt Lake on Wednesday night, after Luc de Fougerolles put RSL ahead in the 79th minute. The Earthquakes, fourth in the Western Conference, have gone eight games without a loss and host Nashville on Saturday with a playoff spot within reach. The Warriors have one preseason game left before their Oct. 21 opener at the Lakers, and the 49ers host Washington on Monday night without the suspended Dre Greenlaw.

stories.t: 49ers punter Corliss Waitman named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week
stories.s: Waitman earned the weekly honor for his work in Sunday’s 32–29 win at Seattle, which kept San Francisco unbeaten at 5–0 and pushed the team up national power rankings. The 49ers turn their attention to Monday night’s home game against the Washington Commanders at Levi’s Stadium.

stories.t: “The Diplomat” season 4 and the Friday the 13th prequel “Crystal Lake” arrive today
stories.s: Netflix releases all eight episodes of The Diplomat’s fourth season, in which a single catastrophe upends Kate Wyler’s fragile US–UK peace and her marriage. Peacock drops all eight episodes of Crystal Lake, starring Linda Cardellini as a grieving Pam Voorhees, and Netflix also premieres the Victorious spinoff Hollywood Arts. Tonight ABC brings back 9-1-1, 9-1-1: Nashville and Grey’s Anatomy.

stories.t: “Street Fighter” leads a crowded weekend with a $25 million to $35 million forecast
stories.s: Paramount’s Street Fighter, directed by Kitao Sakurai and starring Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji, is projected to open with $25 million to $35 million in about 3,500 theaters. It faces Whalefall ($10 million to $12 million forecast), A24’s documentary You Can See Everything ($7 million to $8 million) and a new Sense and Sensibility ($5 million to $8 million).

stories.t: Netflix to cut about 1,000 jobs, roughly 6% of its staff
stories.s: Netflix is laying off about 1,000 employees, mostly in product, technology, legal and human resources, according to an internal memo from co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters first reported by The Wall Street Journal. The company said it remains on track for its full-year forecast as it competes with YouTube, TikTok and other apps for viewers’ attention.

stories.t: YouTube Music starts labeling AI-generated songs
stories.s: YouTube Music is adding labels that show whether a track is fully AI-generated, partly AI-generated or made without generative AI, with details a tap away on the player page; the labels will also come to the main YouTube app. Music partners declare their AI use, backed by YouTube’s own detection tools, and AI tracks can still earn money. Spotify already labels AI music, and Deezer is building a filter to hide it.

stories.t: Artemis II’s Christina Koch steps down from spaceflight to become NASA’s acting deputy chief engineer
stories.s: Koch, who flew around the Moon on Artemis II this year and holds the record for the longest spaceflight by a woman at 328 days, will take the engineering post on Nov. 1 and will no longer be eligible for flight assignments. With her move, all four Artemis II crew members have now left active flight duty.

stories.t: Today in history: The Graf Zeppelin crosses the Atlantic
stories.s: 1928: The German airship Graf Zeppelin landed in Lakehurst, New Jersey, completing its first trip across the Atlantic.

stories.t: On this day in science: A key step toward the birth control pill
stories.s: 1951: Mexican chemist Luis E. Miramontes synthesized norethindrone, a compound that became central to the first oral contraceptives.

stories.t: Firsts in history: China sends its first astronaut to orbit
stories.s: 2003: Yang Liwei circled Earth 14 times aboard Shenzhou 5, making China the third country to launch a person into space on its own.

stories.t: PG&E warns about 70,000 customers of power shutoffs starting Wednesday evening
stories.s: PG&E told roughly 70,000 customers in 29 counties, including more than 4,700 in Alameda County and 1,600 in Contra Costa County, that it may cut power starting around 5:30 p.m. Wednesday because strong winds could bring down lines and spark wildfires. The outages could last until Saturday afternoon, and the areas affected may shift with the forecast.
stories.w: San Mateo County isn’t named in the warning, but the list can change with the weather, so Peninsula residents should check their address with PG&E.

stories.t: Justice Department gives California 48 hours to verify voter citizenship
stories.s: The Justice Department gave California 48 hours to verify the citizenship of voters it has flagged or face federal legal action, according to a letter reported by Reuters. The demand comes three weeks before the Nov. 3 election and follows July letters warning election officials in all 50 states that they could be prosecuted if they knowingly let noncitizens stay on the rolls or vote.
stories.w: San Mateo County voters can check their own ballot’s status with the state’s free Where’s My Ballot service while the dispute plays out.

stories.t: Bipartisan push for kids’ online safety rules grows as Meta lobbies for its own approach
stories.s: Lawmakers from both parties, state attorneys general, school districts and public health groups are pressing for limits on social media companies, and Congress is edging closer to the Kids Online Safety Act, an earlier version of which passed the Senate with 91 votes. Meta opposes blanket bans for kids and has spent $10 million on ads for its teen accounts, while the ACLU warns that age checks could threaten speech and privacy.
stories.w: New federal rules would shape what Bay Area kids see online and would fall heavily on Menlo Park-based Meta.

stories.t: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer after surgery
stories.s: The Vatican said Pope Leo XIV, 71, has lung adenocarcinoma, confirmed during a roughly 90-minute operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital that removed the lower lobe of his right lung. Doctors called the surgery successful and the prognosis excellent because the cancer was caught early, and his audiences are canceled through Oct. 20.
stories.w: The health of the first American pope is closely followed by the Bay Area’s large Catholic community, including parishes across San Mateo County.

stories.t: Russian strikes leave 600,000 Ukrainians without power despite a declared energy truce
stories.s: Russia fired about 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones at Ukraine overnight, leaving at least 600,000 people without power early Wednesday and killing at least one person in Kyiv, the city’s mayor said. President Trump had announced an energy ceasefire on Sunday, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes deliberately targeted energy sites covered by it.
stories.w: Attacks on energy infrastructure keep global fuel markets jittery, which feeds into the gas prices Californians pay.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors rally past the Lakers in Las Vegas; Quakes visit Salt Lake tonight
stories.s: Golden State erased a 13-point halftime deficit to beat the Lakers 101–89 in Las Vegas on Tuesday, holding Los Angeles to 13 points in each of the last two quarters and improving to 3–2 in the preseason. Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski scored 17 points each and Steph Curry added 11 in 22 minutes, though Lendeborg sat out the fourth quarter after appearing to twist his left ankle. The Earthquakes play at Real Salt Lake tonight, and the 49ers host Washington on Monday night.

stories.t: Greenlaw loses his appeal and will miss Monday night’s game against Washington
stories.s: A hearing officer appointed jointly by the NFL and the players’ union upheld linebacker Dre Greenlaw’s one-game suspension for headbutting Seattle’s Ernest Jones IV during Sunday’s 32–29 win. Greenlaw, the 49ers’ second-leading tackler with 37 stops and a forced fumble, will sit out the Week 6 Monday night game against the Commanders at Levi’s Stadium. He can rejoin the active roster the next day.

stories.t: “Resident Evil” becomes the franchise’s biggest film worldwide
stories.s: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil reboot from Sony has earned about $323 million worldwide, the most of the series’ eight films, including roughly $141 million in North America since its Sept. 18 opening. It added an estimated $62.6 million globally last weekend, most of it overseas, where it also topped China’s box office.

stories.t: “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” trailer previews a new Night City story ahead of its Netflix debut
stories.s: Studio Trigger’s anime sequel tells a standalone story with new characters, including a veteran mercenary haunted by his reputation, a netrunner hunting his clan’s killer and a young filmmaker documenting real lives. Kai Ikarashi directs, and the series arrives on Netflix on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

stories.t: “Blue Eye Samurai” adds Jonathan Pryce, Joel Kim Booster and Sherry Cola for season 2
stories.s: The new voice cast was announced at IGN Fan Fest: Pryce as Old Violet, Booster as Priest Ando and Cola as Kuma. The animated Netflix series’ second season is due in January 2027, with a third and final season planned for 2028.

stories.t: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon for Pro and Ultra subscribers
stories.s: Google’s newest frontier model is available now to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in Search, and to developers at an introductory $2 per million input tokens through Nov. 30. Google says Argon is built for long, multi-step work like coding and financial or legal analysis, writes with less hedging, and better resists prompt-injection attacks. GitHub also added Argon to Copilot for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users.

stories.t: NASA finishes stacking the Artemis III boosters at Kennedy
stories.s: Teams at Kennedy Space Center completed the solid rocket booster segments and nose cones for Artemis III, and all four RS-25 engines are now installed on the core stage. In the coming weeks the core stage will be joined to the boosters, and NASA then plans to roll the partial stack to Launch Pad 39B for a fueling test while the four-person crew rehearses launch day.

stories.t: Perseverance breaks Opportunity’s record for the longest drive on another world
stories.s: NASA’s Perseverance rover passed 28.10 miles on Mars on Oct. 11, edging out the 28.06-mile record that Opportunity took about 14 years to set; Perseverance did it in about five and a half. The rover is heading south along the rim of Jezero Crater toward an area that may hold clay minerals formed by water, a key target in the search for signs of past life.

stories.t: Today in history: Winnie-the-Pooh arrives
stories.s: 1926: A.A. Milne published Winnie-the-Pooh, introducing readers to the honey-loving bear and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood.

stories.t: On this day in science: Endeavour reaches its California home
stories.s: 2012: After a slow crawl through Los Angeles streets, the retired space shuttle Endeavour arrived at the California Science Center for display.

stories.t: Firsts in history: Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier
stories.s: 1947: Flying the Bell X-1 high over California’s Mojave Desert, Chuck Yeager became the first person to fly faster than sound.

stories.t: Former 49ers executive and a contractor charged in $1.4 million Event Center kickback case
stories.s: Prosecutors say a former longtime 49ers executive, hired in 2024 to oversee three county-funded construction projects at the San Mateo County Event Center, steered the work to a childhood friend who then kicked back part of the payments. A grand jury indicted both men on 20 counts of commercial burglary each, covering about $1.4 million; both pleaded not guilty and are being held on $750,000 bail. The case surfaced when a construction company told the county it hadn’t been paid.
stories.w: Each Event Center project was paid for with $1 million in county money, so the case puts San Mateo County’s oversight of taxpayer-funded contracts under scrutiny.

stories.t: Peninsula sales taxes could top 10% if the regional transit tax passes
stories.s: The Nov. 3 regional transit measure would add a half-cent sales tax for 14 years in San Mateo, Santa Clara, Alameda and Contra Costa counties, and a full cent in San Francisco, to fund BART, Caltrain, Muni and other agencies. Stacked on local measures, rates in several Peninsula cities would pass 10%: Redwood City and Belmont would rise from 9.875% to 10.375%, and San Carlos could reach 10.375% if its own city tax also passes.
stories.w: Every San Mateo County city, Millbrae included, would pay the extra half-cent on most purchases if the transit tax is approved.

stories.t: BART will test its quake warning system during Thursday’s ShakeOut drill
stories.s: At 10:15 a.m. Thursday, BART will trigger its ShakeAlert early-warning system as part of the International ShakeOut drill, so trains will slow to 27 mph and make a very brief stop. Crews will run simulated damage inspections at all 50 stations, and riders will hear a systemwide reminder to prepare for earthquakes. BART’s advice: sit down or hold on if a quake hits, stay back from the platform edge, and text family instead of calling.
stories.w: Riders on the Millbrae and SFO lines should expect a brief slowdown mid-morning Thursday, and it’s a good prompt to review your own quake plan.

stories.t: PG&E restores power after a weekend of wildfire-safety shutoffs
stories.s: PG&E cut power Friday in parts of Fresno, Kern, San Luis Obispo and other counties, restored it Saturday, then shut off roughly 11,000 customers in counties including Shasta, Tehama and Yolo on Sunday as fire risk rose. The utility issued weather all-clears by early Monday afternoon and said every affected customer had power back by 8 p.m. Monday. Alameda, Napa and Solano were in the initial scope, but San Mateo County was not.
stories.w: San Mateo County wasn’t affected, but fall shutoffs can reach the Bay Area, so it’s worth checking your address on PG&E’s outage site and keeping backup power ready.

stories.t: Houthi missiles target Riyadh for a third straight day
stories.s: The Saudi-led coalition said Monday it intercepted a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh and two more aimed at Khamis Mushait, a day after a strike on King Khalid International Airport killed one person and wounded 11. A Houthi attack on the airport Saturday killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300; the airport will stay closed until at least this Saturday, and several airlines have canceled Riyadh flights.
stories.w: The fighting is part of the wider regional conflict around the war with Iran, which keeps oil prices high and feeds the gas prices Bay Area drivers pay.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers stay perfect; Warriors meet the Lakers in Las Vegas tonight
stories.s: The 49ers held on for a 32–29 win at Seattle on Sunday to improve to 5–0, with Mike Evans catching seven passes for 113 yards and a touchdown and Renardo Green picking off two passes; they host Washington next Monday night. The Earthquakes drew 1–1 at Colorado on Saturday, stretching their unbeaten run to seven before Wednesday’s trip to Real Salt Lake. Tonight the Warriors play the Lakers in a preseason game at T-Mobile Arena at 7 p.m. Pacific on NBA TV, still without Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody, who are out with knee injuries.

stories.t: NFL suspends 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw one game for headbutting a Seahawk
stories.s: Greenlaw was ejected in the second quarter in Seattle after a late hit on quarterback Sam Darnold sparked a sideline scuffle, during which he headbutted linebacker Ernest Jones IV, who wasn’t wearing a helmet. The league suspended him for next Monday night’s home game against Washington, pending an appeal set for Tuesday. Greenlaw, who rejoined San Francisco this season, has 37 tackles in five games, and coach Kyle Shanahan said he was disappointed by the decision.

stories.t: Jessica Chastain’s “Other Mommy” opens at No. 1 with $27.5 million
stories.s: Universal’s horror film led the weekend with an estimated $27.5 million in North America and about $45.2 million worldwide, well ahead of its reported $18 million budget. The Social Reckoning opened in fifth place with $5.5 million domestically. Both numbers are studio estimates, with final figures due early this week.

stories.t: Marvel’s “VisionQuest” premieres on Disney+ tonight
stories.s: Paul Bettany returns as Vision in the eight-episode series, which debuts with two episodes at 6 p.m. Pacific on Tuesday. New episodes arrive in pairs on Tuesdays, and the episode titles, from “No Strings” to “Forever,” hint at a story about identity, corruption and starting over.

stories.t: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier AI model
stories.s: Meta’s Superintelligence Lab launched Muse Wonder and the more powerful Muse Wonder Full, which Meta says perform comparably to rivals’ top models and lead a benchmark for remembering and using what users tell them. Developers can use Muse Wonder through Meta’s API at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, while Muse Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code subscribers. Both models will power Meta’s Muse agent.

stories.t: SpaceX set to launch a cargo Dragon with the station’s last new solar arrays
stories.s: A Falcon 9 was scheduled to lift off from Cape Canaveral at 3:35 a.m. Pacific on Tuesday with about 6,300 pounds of supplies for the International Space Station on the CRS-35 mission. The cargo includes the final set of roll-out solar arrays for the station, plus experiments on artificial retinas, 3D heart tissue and brain organoids. The capsule is due to dock on its own Thursday morning.

stories.t: Today in history: The White House gets its cornerstone
stories.s: 1792: Builders laid the cornerstone of the White House, the presidential home that would first be occupied in 1800.

stories.t: On this day in science: Carbon dating puts the Shroud of Turin in the Middle Ages
stories.s: 1988: The archbishop of Turin announced that radiocarbon tests dated the famous Shroud of Turin to the Middle Ages.

stories.t: Firsts in history: Boston wins the first modern World Series
stories.s: 1903: The Boston Americans beat the Pittsburgh Pirates to take the first modern World Series.

stories.t: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home in a criminal investigation
stories.s: Homeland Security Investigations agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington-area home early Monday under a court-approved warrant in what the Justice Department called an ongoing criminal investigation; sources told ABC News it concerns her immigration paperwork. Omar, who hasn’t been charged and denies wrongdoing, called it an attack on political enemies, and the search comes 22 days before the midterms despite DOJ guidance against overt steps close to an election.
stories.w: It raises fresh questions about federal investigations of members of Congress in the final weeks before an election in which Bay Area voters are also choosing their representatives.

stories.t: SF Democrats drop Yekutiel endorsement and back Gary McCoy for District 8
stories.s: At an emergency meeting Sunday, the San Francisco Democratic Party voted 29-0 to rescind its endorsement of Manny Yekutiel, who left the District 8 supervisor race after a second sexual-assault allegation was published Oct. 1, then voted to endorse Gary McCoy. Party chair Nancy Tung apologized for how the party handled the allegations, and one member resigned during the meeting.
stories.w: San Francisco’s Board of Supervisors also governs SFO, which sits in San Mateo County, so the board’s makeup matters to Peninsula residents too.

stories.t: Trump administration weighs firing Kimberly Guilfoyle as ambassador to Greece
stories.s: President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are considering removing Kimberly Guilfoyle as ambassador to Greece, AP reported, following Wall Street Journal reports that she asked a donor to pay a $100,000 credit card bill and accepted improper gifts. Her lawyers deny wrongdoing, and a decision could come after the Columbus Day holiday.
stories.w: Guilfoyle is a former California prosecutor with long ties to San Francisco politics, so the case is drawing attention around the Bay Area.

stories.t: Weekend recap: 49ers stay perfect with a wild win in Seattle
stories.s: The 49ers beat the Seahawks 32-29 on Sunday to reach 5-0 and take a two-game lead in the NFC West. On Saturday the Warriors topped Sacramento 111-106 in the preseason and the Earthquakes drew 1-1 with Colorado, and on Friday the Valkyries swept Las Vegas to reach the WNBA Finals. This week: the Warriors face the Lakers Tuesday, the Earthquakes host Real Salt Lake Wednesday, the Valkyries open the Finals at Chase Center Saturday, and the 49ers host Washington on Monday night, Oct. 19.

stories.t: Seven turnovers and a late kick: how the 49ers outlasted Seattle
stories.s: Eddy Pineiro’s field goal with 1:56 left won a game that featured an NFL season-high seven combined turnovers, and Malik Mustapha stopped Cooper Kupp a yard short on fourth down to seal it. Brock Purdy threw for 189 yards and two touchdowns, including a go-ahead pass to Brandin Cooks, but Deebo Samuel left with a strained hamstring and linebacker Dre Greenlaw was ejected.

stories.t: Oakland Roots say goodbye to the Coliseum with a scoreless draw
stories.s: The Oakland Roots played their last match at the Oakland Coliseum on Saturday, a 0-0 draw with San Antonio FC in front of 9,718 fans, after citing costs and limits on how they could run game days. The club hasn’t named a 2027 home, though it’s looking at an Alameda training site in the short term and Howard Terminal in the long run.

stories.t: Sorkin’s ‘The Social Reckoning’ stumbles at the box office
stories.s: Aaron Sorkin’s Facebook whistleblower drama was on track for about $5.5 million in its opening weekend, below the studio’s $7 million to $8 million projection and far behind the $22 million debut of ‘The Social Network’ in 2010. Alex Gibney’s four-hour ‘Musk’ documentary took in about $69,000 in four theaters ahead of a wider rollout and a stop on HBO Max.

stories.t: Golden Gate Bridge-era drama ‘Fog City’ films in San Francisco
stories.s: ‘Fog City,’ a movie set during the 1930s construction of the Golden Gate Bridge, has taken over two blocks of Steiner Street for a shoot that runs through Monday. Daniel Pritzker directs and co-wrote it, and the cast reportedly includes Miranda Otto, Cooper Koch and Angus Imrie.

stories.t: Apple expected to unveil a Siri-powered home hub on Tuesday
stories.s: Bloomberg reports Apple will announce HomeView, a smart home hub with a display, an A18 chip and Siri, in countertop and wall-mounted versions, along with updated Apple TV and HomePod mini models. Apple is also expected to reveal a smart lock, thermostat and doorbell partnership with LG.

stories.t: Amazon drops secrecy deals for data centers as local opposition grows
stories.s: Amazon says it will stop using nondisclosure agreements when negotiating data center projects with local governments, following a similar move by Microsoft earlier this year. The change comes as many communities, including San Francisco, pass moratoriums over worries about electricity bills, water use and property values.

stories.t: TechCrunch Disrupt opens Tuesday at Moscone West
stories.s: TechCrunch’s annual startup conference runs Oct. 13–15 in San Francisco, with more than 250 speakers across 200-plus sessions. Twenty Startup Battlefield finalists will compete live for a $100,000 prize.

stories.t: Today in history: Khrushchev’s famous shoe moment
stories.s: 1960: During a heated Cold War session at the United Nations, Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev reportedly banged his shoe in protest, a scene still debated today.

stories.t: On this day in science: Voskhod 1 carries a crew of three
stories.s: 1964: The Soviet Union launched Voskhod 1, the first spacecraft to carry more than one person, with a commander, an engineer and a doctor aboard.

stories.t: Firsts in history: The very first Oktoberfest
stories.s: 1810: Munich held the first Oktoberfest, a horse race celebrating a royal wedding that grew into the world’s best-known beer festival.

stories.t: Pope Leo XIV to have surgery to remove a lung nodule
stories.s: Pope Leo XIV, 71, said at his Sunday blessing that he will have surgery early this week to remove a lesion found on his lung during recent checkups, adding that it was caught at an early stage. The Vatican expects about a week of recovery, and the pope says he still plans to make a Nov. 6–17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.
stories.w: The first American pope has a large following among Bay Area Catholics, including parishes across San Mateo County in the Archdiocese of San Francisco.

stories.t: Nine dead after a shooting at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania
stories.s: Police say a gunman fired shots outside an Erie home on Friday evening, killing two women in the street, then went inside, where officers later found more victims, including children, and the gunman dead of an apparent self-inflicted wound. Nine people died in all, and the police chief said there is no ongoing threat while investigators work to find a motive.
stories.w: It ranks among the deadliest U.S. shootings this year and is likely to sharpen gun-policy debates ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

stories.t: Pentagon plans to livestream the Fort Hood shooter’s execution, drawing pushback
stories.s: The Pentagon confirmed that the December firing-squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, will be streamed online. Vice President JD Vance said he doubts the livestream will happen and won’t watch if it does, and the head of the U.S. Catholic bishops urged officials to reconsider.
stories.w: It would be an unprecedented public broadcast of a U.S. execution, just as Gov. Newsom weighs ending California’s death sentences altogether.

stories.t: Honors classes split the Sequoia high school board race
stories.s: The race for the Sequoia Union High School District seat covering Belmont, San Carlos and part of Redwood City pits incumbent Amy Koo against Belmont parent Alon Shiran, and the main dividing line is the district’s 2023 removal of some ninth- and tenth-grade honors classes. Shiran wants the courses back, while Koo, who voted to cut them, says the change has eased freshmen’s move to high school; two current board members already favor bringing them back.
stories.w: The district serves about 9,000 San Mateo County students from Belmont to East Palo Alto, and this seat could decide whether honors options return.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers put their perfect record on the line in Seattle
stories.s: The 4-0 49ers visit the 3-1 Seahawks at Lumen Field today at 1:25 p.m. on FOX, a week after beating Denver. Seattle is a 3-point favorite, and San Francisco brings the NFL’s best third-down conversion rate (57.5%) against a Seahawks defense allowing 18.25 points a game.

stories.t: Valkyries sweep the Aces to reach their first WNBA Finals
stories.s: The Golden State Valkyries beat the defending champion Las Vegas Aces 87-77 in overtime on Friday to finish a 3-0 semifinal sweep. They open the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center on Saturday, Oct. 17.

stories.t: Paramount closes its Warner Bros. Discovery takeover, creating a new media giant
stories.s: Paramount’s purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed on Oct. 6 after a yearlong fight that included a rival Netflix bid and a lawsuit from 12 state attorneys general, creating a company now called Skydance with nearly $70 billion in yearly revenue. Paramount+, HBO Max and Discovery+ are expected to merge eventually, and leadership has warned of significant job cuts.

stories.t: Nathan Fielder co-directs a Theranos documentary opening Thursday
stories.s: ‘You Can See Everything,’ a documentary about Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos from Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, opens in theaters Oct. 15. A tie-in website lets visitors poke around a re-creation of Holmes’s desk at the company and read her emails.

stories.t: Microsoft’s Nadella calls for an ‘emergency brake’ on AI models
stories.s: In a Saturday post on X, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella urged the industry to keep safety controls outside AI models, record every significant model action in tamper-resistant logs, and make sure a person can pause or stop a model mid-task. His comments follow a string of cases in which AI companies reported losing control of how their models behaved.

stories.t: Apple hires the team behind AI podcast app Huxe
stories.s: A filing with the European Commission shows Apple agreed to hire some Huxe AI employees and license its technology; the startup was founded by developers behind Google’s AI-generated podcast feature in NotebookLM and shut down its app in May. Apple hasn’t said how it will use the technology, though it could bring AI-generated audio to Apple Podcasts.

stories.t: Today in history: Saturday Night Live goes on the air
stories.s: 1975: NBC aired the first episode of Saturday Night Live, the late-night sketch show that is still running decades later.

stories.t: On this day in science: Pioneer 1 heads for the Moon
stories.s: 1958: The U.S. launched the uncrewed probe Pioneer 1 toward lunar orbit, one of the earliest attempts to send a spacecraft to the Moon.

stories.t: Firsts in history: An American woman walks in space
stories.s: 1984: Astronaut Kathryn Sullivan stepped outside the space shuttle Challenger, becoming the first American woman to walk in space.

stories.t: Hurricane Isaias slams the Florida Panhandle, cutting power to nearly 700,000
stories.s: Isaias came ashore near Destin, Florida, around 8 p.m. Eastern on Friday as a Category 2 storm after briefly reaching Category 3, and more than 697,000 customers lost power across Florida, Alabama and Georgia. It was the season’s first Atlantic hurricane, the latest first hurricane in 121 years, and it is expected to weaken as it moves north through Alabama and the Tennessee Valley this weekend.
stories.w: Flights between SFO and Gulf Coast or Southeast airports may be disrupted this weekend, so check before heading out.

stories.t: New state law lets San Mateo County keep young kids off e-bikes
stories.s: Gov.
